question: What does the Happiness Index primarily measure?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Subjective well-being**__.

**__Key Points__**
__

• The **World Happiness Report** primarily measures **Subjective well-being**, which refers to how individuals evaluate their own lives and experience their daily existence. It is a self-reported metric that captures the emotional and cognitive evaluations of a person's life quality.

• The core measurement is based on the **Cantril Ladder** survey question, where respondents are asked to imagine a ladder with steps numbered from **0 to 10**. They rate their current life on this scale, where **10** is the best possible life and **0** is the worst. ***Hence, the correct answer is Subjective well-being.***

• **National income** (Option 1) is often measured by **Gross Domestic Product (GDP)**. While the report uses **GDP per capita** as one of the six explanatory variables to understand why some countries are happier than others, it is not the primary definition of happiness itself. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***

• **Industrial growth** (Option 2) focuses on the expansion of the manufacturing and industrial sectors of an economy. While it contributes to economic development, it does not directly account for the social, psychological, or emotional health of the citizenry. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***

• **Population density** (Option 4) measures the number of people living per unit of area. There is no direct or consistent correlation between the number of people in a given space and their reported levels of happiness or life satisfaction. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

**Additional Information__**
__

• The **World Happiness Report** is an annual publication of the **United Nations Sustainable Development Solutions Network (SDSN)**. The first report was released in **April 2012** to support the **UN High-Level Meeting** on **Happiness and Well-Being**.

• The global movement to measure happiness was significantly influenced by the **Kingdom of Bhutan**. In the **1970s**, **King Jigme Singye Wangchuck** famously declared that **Gross National Happiness (GNH)** is more important than **Gross National Product (GNP)**.

• The data used for the rankings is primarily sourced from the **Gallup World Poll**, which conducts surveys in more than **150 countries** worldwide, using a sample size of approximately **1,000 respondents** per country.

• **Finland** has consistently secured the **1st rank** as the world's happiest country for **seven consecutive years** (from **2018 to 2024**). This is often attributed to the country's strong **social safety nets**, high levels of **social trust**, and effective **public services**.

• The report serves as a tool for **policymakers** and **governments** to shift their focus from purely economic indicators to more human-centric development goals, emphasizing **mental health**, **social support**, and **environmental sustainability**.

**Important Points__**

• To explain the differences in happiness scores across different nations, the report analyzes **six key variables**: **GDP per capita**, **Social support** (having someone to count on in times of trouble), **Healthy life expectancy** at birth, **Freedom to make life choices**, **Generosity** (measured by recent donations), and **Perceptions of corruption** in government and business.

• The **2024 World Happiness Report** highlighted a growing trend of 'happiness inequality', noting that in many regions, the gap between the happiest and least happy individuals within the same **country** is widening.

• Recent editions of the report have also explored the impact of **digital technology**, **social media**, and global events like the **COVID-19 pandemic** on the **subjective well-being** of different age groups, particularly the **youth** and the **elderly**.

• The **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)**, specifically **Goal 3** (Good Health and Well-being), align with the objectives of the **Happiness Index** by promoting holistic development that includes mental and emotional health.
